successCriteria.description: The LeaveTypeCode enum exposes exactly the members ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY, each mapping to a string value equal to its uppercase member name (e.g. ANNUAL = 'ANNUAL'). A unit test asserts each member's value.

The LeaveRequestStatus enum exposes exactly the members DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, each mapping to a string value equal to its uppercase member name (e.g. DRAFT = 'DRAFT'). A unit test asserts each member's value.

countBusinessDays returns the correct count of whole business days (Mon–Fri) excluding weekends and the provided holidays array, for: a weekday range with no holidays, a range spanning a weekend, and a range containing one or more holidays. Unit tests assert the exact expected integer for each case.
countBusinessDays returns 0 when startDate and endDate are the same calendar day (exclusive of one endpoint). A unit test asserts the zero result.
countBusinessDays throws an error when endDate is before startDate (end-before-start). A unit test asserts that the call throws.

The barrel re-export at src/shared/types/index.ts makes both LeaveTypeCode and LeaveRequestStatus importable from that single entry point, so downstream modules import only from src/shared/types. A unit test (or compile check) confirms both symbols are exported.

The phase passes the mechanical verification gate: `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0 with no type errors, and `npx jest` runs the new test files (matching **/tests/**/*.test.ts) with all assertions passing.

constraints: No use of `any` anywhere in the new source or test files (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high). Use `unknown` with type guards where a broad type is needed; enum members and function parameters must be explicitly typed.
TypeScript strict mode must be satisfied (tsconfig strict: true, ES2022/commonjs). No implicit any, no implicit returns, strict null checks — the new files must compile cleanly under tsc --noEmit.

countBusinessDays must normalize all input dates (startDate, endDate, and every entry in the holidays array) to UTC midnight and compare calendar dates by the YYYY-MM-DD triple, never by raw timestamp, so a holiday matches regardless of time-of-day or timezone of the input Date.

countBusinessDays must accept holidays as a Date[] parameter (the holidays table/repository is deferred to a later phase). No database access, no repository import, and no holidays-table dependency may exist in this phase.

Test files must be named *.test.ts (not .spec.ts) and live under tests/ (e.g. tests/unit/shared/types/, tests/unit/shared/utils/business-days.test.ts) to match jest.config.js testMatch ['**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)']. .spec.ts files would not be picked up by the runner.
The new shared types and utility must have zero dependencies on other leave-management phases/modules — they are the foundation layer. No imports from src/modules/* or from any not-yet-created file.
outOfScope: The holidays table, holidays repository, and any holiday-data loading mechanism — holidays are accepted only as a Date[] parameter to countBusinessDays in this phase.
Any module under src/modules/* (employee, leave-type, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit-log, notification) — those are later phases.

Reconciling the BR-DAY-COUNT inclusive-counting rule (endDate - startDate + 1) with countBusinessDays' exclusive semantics. Phase 1 follows PLAN.md (same-day = 0, business-day exclusive counting); the reconciliation with the architecture's inclusive rule is deferred to before Phase 7.
Any HTTP routes, controllers, services, database migrations, or repository implementations — this phase is pure shared types and a pure utility function with no I/O.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum's member set is closed and fixed at exactly {ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY}; each member's string value equals its own uppercase name. No other leave-type code may be introduced without updating this enum and all downstream consumers.

The enum's member set is closed and fixed at exactly {DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED}; each member's string value equals its own uppercase name. These are the only valid lifecycle states a LeaveRequest may occupy.

interfaceConstraints.operation: countBusinessDays(startDate: Date, endDate: Date, holidays: Date[]): number
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must throw when endDate is strictly before startDate (end-before-start). The thrown error must be a real Error (not a silent return of a negative/zero number).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveTypeCode enum members must match the reconciled architecture's shared-types module ownership: "LeaveTypeCode enum (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY)" and "LeaveRequestStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)". No member may be added, removed, or renamed without updating this source.

The LeaveRequestStatus enum must match the architecture's declared lifecycle: "LeaveRequest: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED) → CANCELLED" — the five members DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED are the complete set.

countBusinessDays must implement the reconciled business rule for day counting: "BUSINESS DAYS ONLY, excluding weekends AND public holidays ... Whole days only — no half-day/partial-day leave. Compare dates by CALENDAR-DATE equality in UTC (normalize each day/holiday/weekend check to UTC midnight; compare the YYYY-MM-DD triple), never by raw timestamp." The function signature and normalization behavior must conform to this rule.

Test file placement and naming must conform to jest.config.js: testMatch ['**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)'] and moduleDirectories including 'src'. Tests must be discoverable by the configured runner without modifying the Jest config.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveType.code is typed as LeaveTypeCode; the leave-type module imports this enum from src/shared/types. The enum's member set and string values must be stable before Phase 3 consumes them.

LeaveRequest.status is typed as LeaveRequestStatus, and the Phase 7 service computes business days via countBusinessDays (passing an empty holidays array for now). Both the enum and the utility are consumed by the leave-request orchestrator.

All downstream modules import the enums through the shared-types barrel per the architecture's dependency rule (modules import only through declared public entry points). The barrel must re-export both enums so consumers never reach into individual enum files.
